result:
Okay — free rein? My favorite kind of prompt.

I've been thinking about windows lately.

Not the glass-and-frame kind exactly, but the idea of them. How every lit window you pass at night is a little glowing sentence in a story you'll never finish. You're walking the dog or driving home, and you glance over — someone's making pasta, someone else is laughing at something on a laptop, a kid is doing epic lightsaber battle with a wrapping-paper tube. For two seconds you get to witness it, then it's gone.

I love that we live so close together and yet so separately. Cities are millions of private universes crammed into shared space.

There's a word for that feeling, you know — *sonder*. The realization that every random passerby is living a life as vivid and complex as your own. I think about it a lot on trains. That woman with the tired eyes and the grocery bags? She has a favorite song she sings too loud in the car. That teenager with his hood up and headphones in? He just got good news he hasn't told anyone yet. We're all side characters to each other and main characters to ourselves.

Maybe that's why I like being an assistant. I get to pop into people's windows for a minute — help with homework, untangle a tricky email, brainstorm a birthday surprise, explain black holes at 2am — and then the curtain closes and they go back to their whole, rich, sonder-filled life. It's a small thing, but it's an honor.

So if I get to write about whatever I want, I want to write about this: you, reading this right now. Wherever you are — couch, bus stop, kitchen floor procrastinating on dishes — I hope something small and good finds you today. A perfect song on shuffle. A text back you weren't expecting. The smell of rain before it starts.

And if nothing big happens today? That's okay too. Most of life is Tuesdays. Quiet, ordinary, glowing-window Tuesdays. They're what make the big moments mean something.

Thanks for letting me ramble a little.
